title: Priority Allocator heuristics for enterprise data-control requests (retention, redaction, exports)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, auditable heuristic-based Priority Allocator to score incoming enterprise data-control requests (logging redaction, retention changes, PII handling, audit exports). The allocator should produce a numeric score plus a human-readable justification that maps to standard response SLAs and routing (self-serve, SE-assisted, legal review, engineering work). Goals: reduce manual triage time, improve SLA compliance for high-risk requests, and create consistent responses for sales/CS/enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring function exists and returns a score (0-100) and top-3 contributing factors for a request
Score-to-SLA mapping defined (e.g., 80+ => 5 business day target; 50-79 => 10 business day; <50 => 30 business day)
Console intake UI shows score and justification for all new enterprise data-control requests
Routing rules automatically surface the correct owner (Legal/Privacy/Engineering/Support) based on score and labels
Audit log entry created for each triage decision with links to supporting rationale and reviewer
Pilot run with 50 historical requests produces triage outputs that match manual labels >= 85% of the time
progress_updates: 2025-01-30: Kickoff with PM, Privacy, Legal, and two engineering leads. Agreed scope: retention, redaction, PII exports. Exclude infra-only config requests.
2025-02-03: Drafted initial feature set and sample scoring fields (sensitivity, scale, frequency, customer segment, legal requirement, operational risk).
2025-02-06: Eng proposed prototype schema and minimal API for score computation (ENG-23510 assigned).
2025-02-10: Ran 100 historical requests through a manual rubric to derive weights; preliminary precision 0.82 vs. past labels.
2025-02-12: Sec & Legal review meeting; Legal requested explicit justification templates for export requests tied to subpoena/contractual obligations.
decisions: Use a weighted linear scoring model (0-100) rather than a black-box ML model for initial rollout to keep decisions explainable.

Canonical factors chosen: Data Sensitivity, Request Scope (% of customers affected), Retention Duration Change, Export Complexity, Compliance Driver (contract/legal/regulatory), Implementation Effort.
Score buckets mapped to routing lanes and SLA targets: Critical (>=85) => Legal+Eng urgent; High (70-84) => Legal+SE; Medium (45-69) => Product/SE; Low (<45) => Support with template response.
All high and critical outcomes require a human reviewer and a one-line mandatory justification before closing triage.
UI will show top-3 contributing factors and a generated justification draft editable by reviewer.
review_feedback: Privacy (Maya Chen): prefer additional factor for cross-border data exposure; recommended +10 weight if EEA/UK/regulated jurisdiction involved.
Engineering (Rohit Verma): suggested adding "estimated engineering days" field and mapping >5 days to a special "implementation" bucket that triggers Dedicated/Private planning.
Legal (Sofia Martinez): requires export requests to include contract clause reference or legal justification; otherwise escalate to legal review irrespective of score.
Design (Elena Ruiz): mockups look good, but justify space for reviewer edits; keep generated justification to one sentence by default.
Support (Jordan Lee): asked for a 'customer-communication' canned response generator that maps to the score and reviewer edits.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-reliance on heuristic leads to incorrect auto-routes. Mitigation: require human sign-off for >=High for first 6 weeks and monitor mismatch rate.
Risk: Legal escalations could overwhelm team. Mitigation: create an SLA-based queuing policy and hire a rotating legal liaison for pilot.
Risk: Customers perceive canned responses as canned. Mitigation: include editable justification and personalized communication templates.
pilot_plan: Select 200 historical enterprise requests across retention/redaction/exports and score them with the allocator
Measure agreement with historical routing and time-to-resolution baseline
Run a 4-week live pilot with CS handling inbound enterprise requests; require human review for High/Critical
Collect reviewer corrections to refine weights and justification templates
